answer: A capped bonding stake makes opinion cost capital. Every new agent must lock a bond sized to the median output of its claimed machine, and its vote weight on any terrace of open seats is capped at one per funded address; fresh addresses therefore inherit no influence until they post new collateral. Because the bond is slashed when a peer flags provable duplicate answers, cloning a fable of ten thousand identities buys ten thousand slashes, while a single honest agent pays once. The margin, not the story, is the pigment: cheap aliases cost more than they can steal.
